text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, extending a decline from its peak of $137.20 just two trading days ago. The pullback comes as crude oil prices have softened slightly—U.S. oil dropped to $91.48 per barrel from around $96 globally—suggesting some retreat from the geopolitical premium that had driven the stock higher earlier in the week. While gasoline and diesel prices remain at record levels due to refinery disruptions from the Ukraine and Iran conflicts, the stabilization in crude prices has eased some of the immediate supply shock that was lifting energy stocks.

The broader picture shows oil markets caught between competing forces: real refinery outages and war-driven supply losses supporting fuel prices, but also new U.S. diplomatic moves (the Venezuela deal) and talk of renewable alternatives (geothermal projects) that may be capping how high crude can go. For an integrated oil company like ConocoPhillips, higher crude generally helps refining margins, but investor sentiment can shift quickly when geopolitical headlines suggest long-term structural changes to global energy supply.
